newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees world 96/97 coffee output 97.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees world 96/97 coffee output 97.6 mln.

text.p: German statistician F.O. Licht on Thursday put world 1996/97 coffee production at 97.6 million bags, up from its November forecast of 96.5 million and 1995/96's 87.7 million.
In its second estimate of world 1996/97 production German-based Licht said the upward revision reflected higher output in the robusta sector.
Licht said robusta production is now forecast to reach 32.57 million bags against its November estimate of 31.67 million. In 1995/96 the robusta crop totalled 29.71 million.
At 65.05 million bags, the arabica total is only marginally higher than was forecast in November of 64.78 million. In 1995/96, arabica production reached 57.97 million.
Licht said Brazil output would total 28.5 million bags in 1996/97 against the weather-hit crop of 15.8 million in 1995/96.
A whole range of problems has hit the Colombian industry and production is expected to fall to 9.6 million from 12.89 million in 1995/96.
It is hoped the steep rise in world market price will help revive the Colombian sector, Licht said.
At 15.5 million bags, Mexico is by far the largest producer in North and Central America even though, reflecting the bi-annual production cycle, it is down by 250,000 bags on the year.
The setback in Guatemala was not so great as had been forecast and output in 1996/97 is now estimated at 3.65 million against 3.9 million last season.
African output is expected to reach nearly 19 million bags this season with robusta coffee accounting for 60 percent of the total.
Forecasts of the Ivorian crop range from 3.8 million to 5.0 million bags, a big jump from last season but wastage and rejection will limit exports.
At nearly 16.5 million bags output in Asia is expected to amount to slightly more than in the previous season.
Statistics from Indonesia vary substantially but output in 1996/97 is expected to reach about 6.5 million bags, up by about 150,000 on the year.

The industry continues to grow in Vietnam and output is now expected to reach 4.5 million bags compared with less than 4.0 million in 1995/96 and roughly double what was achieved only four seasons ago.

Licht said even though statistics point to a sharp increase in 1996/97 production, initial consumption forecasts suggest there would be little, if any, surplus so the stock position would remain highly precarious.
With a good chance that production will fall in both Brazil and Indonesia next season, increases in other producing countries will be needed.
"A frost in Brazil would be the last drop in the bucket," Licht said.
"Highly remunerative prices, especially for arabica producers, appear likely for the remaineder of the year," the firm said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
